titel: Ep. 382 - Summer’s venture wave; drugging beta-catenin; Capricor & FDA

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: Summer biotech venture activity surges, new beta-catenin approaches, and Capricor update
kurzfassung: Despite the summer slowdown, biotech venture rounds brought in nearly $800 million last week, driven by novel startups and cross-border deals. Researchers are pursuing five distinct mechanisms to target the previously undruggable beta-catenin pathway in cancer. Meanwhile, Capricor is refocusing its regulatory strategy for its Duchenne muscular dystrophy therapy following advisory committee feedback.
stichpunkte: Vaderis secured a major round with an oral allosteric AKT inhibitor for a rare disease.
Khartis launched with an oral IGF-1R inhibitor to challenge Amgen's Tepezza.
Boulevard Bio became the fourteenth NewCo of the year licensing assets from Asia and the US.
Five clinical programs are targeting the beta-catenin pathway using distinct peptide and small molecule approaches.
Parabilis advanced its peptide macrocycle into a planned Phase III trial after a record IPO.
Capricor adjusted its BLA approach to pursue approval for Duchenne muscular dystrophy focused on limb function.
BioCentury's upcoming signature issue explores global strategies to expedite first-in-human clinical studies.

clips.hook: Summer venture funding reaches $791 million across 13 rounds
clips.text: Swiss biotech firm Videris secured the largest funding round last week, bringing in $791 million across 13 total deals for its phase three rare disease treatment.

clips.hook: Slate Medicines plans a reverse merger with Fulcrum Therapeutics
clips.text: Slate Medicines is planning a reverse merger with NASDAQ-traded Fulcrum Therapeutics, which recently halted its early-stage sickle cell program.

clips.hook: Why targeting beta-catenin has challenged scientists for years
clips.text: Researchers bypassed the structural challenges of targeting beta-catenin's flat surface by utilizing cell-penetrating peptides.

clips.hook: Advisory committee votes nine to three against cardiomyopathy efficacy
clips.text: Capricor CEO Linda Marban addressed investors last Thursday after an advisory committee voted nine to three against the efficacy of their cardiomyopathy treatment.

clips.hook: China created a new urgency around expediting first-in-human trials
clips.text: Global regulatory hurdles and rapid advancements in China are driving an urgent push to accelerate first-in-human clinical trials for patients.

beschreibung:
A baker’s dozen of biotechs shrugged off the summer haze to raise nearly $800 million in venture cash. On the latest BioCentury This Week podcast, BioCentury’s analysts discuss the financings, which included money for a potential challenger to Amgen’s blockbuster Tepezza and a new venture from immunology professor Georg Schett with backing from Deerfield Management, Boulevard Bio.
The analysts also discuss new approaches to drug cancer’s “undruggable” β-catenin pathway, and whether Capricor’s latest regulatory move will give Duchenne muscular dystrophy therapy deramiocel new life at FDA.
